papers.title: Degenerate complex structures on surfaces and stability conditions
papers.abstract: Physical heuristics suggest that the space of Bridgeland stability conditions of a projective Calabi-Yau manifold $X$ should be related to the moduli space of complex structures on its mirror $X^\vee$. On the other hand, recent work in the literature introduces a modular partial compactification, $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(X)$, of a quotient of the space of stability conditions on $\mathcal{D}^{b}(X)$. We provide some mathematical evidence for the aforementioned heuristics by proving that for curves and surfaces, certain boundary strata in $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ describe degenerate complex structures on $X^\vee$. Along the way, we introduce a criterion for producing boundary points of $\mathcal{A}\mathrm{Stab}(\mathcal{D})$ when $\mathcal{D}$ is an arbitrary $k$-linear triangulated category. As a byproduct, we deduce the existence of Bridgeland stability conditions on certain quotients of the derived categories of K3 and Enriques surfaces.

papers.title: Degeneration of (-1)-shifted symplectic stacks and categorification of Donaldson-Thomas invariants
papers.abstract: We study cohomological Donaldson-Thomas invariants of perfect complexes in a semistable degeneration of projective Calabi-Yau threefolds, with smooth components $X_1,X_2$ meeting along a smooth anticanonical surface $S$. The generic fiber of degeneration family is a $(-1)$-shifted symplectic stack. Over the special fiber, the derived restriction to $S$ is derived Lagrangian, and its homotopy fiber product is also $(-1)$-shifted symplectic. Our goal is to relate the categorical DT invariants of the generic fiber moduli, induced by periodic cyclic homology of matrix factorization category of 0-shifted potential functions over such moduli, to that of the special fiber obtained via derived Lagrangian intersection and geometric quantization. This is achieved via construction of a flat Gauss-Manin connection that relates the generic fiber cohomological DT invariants to that of the special fiber. The geometric framework, universal trace diagrams, and fourfold foliation were developed jointly with Jacob Kryczka in arXiv:2510.20325. Here we construct ordinary critical realizations, oriented cyclic-to-bar comparisons, and Gauss-Manin operators, and verify finite specialization in explicit moduli problems. We workout our construction via several explicit examples such as Grassmannians, Relative Hilbert Schemes and moduli space of pure 2 dimensional sheaves with support moving in a fixed linear system of divisors in the ambient threefold.

papers.title: Moment Polyptychs and the Equivariant Quantisation of Hypertoric Varieties
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant geometric quantisation of a non-compact hypertoric variety of complex dimension $2n$ using symplectic cutting. When the defining arrangement is cooriented so that its base region is non-empty and bounded, fibre rotation has proper moment map and produces compact K\"ahler orbifold cuts carrying the residual torus action. We introduce the moment polyptych of such a cut, a polytopal complex assembled from truncated arrangement regions, and show that its vertices and local lattice data determine the fixed points, tangent weights, and finite orbifold groups required for equivariant orbifold Riemann-Roch localisation. Even for a smooth hypertoric manifold, a reducible core forces every cut in the outer cut chamber to have non-trivial cyclic isotropy, while the cuts are smooth if and only if the manifold is the cotangent bundle of its distinguished compact toric subvariety, which is then a product of projective spaces. For a positive regular integral level $d$ in the outer cut chamber, algebraic cutting identifies the cut's quantisation with a finite filtration piece of the circle-graded quantisation of the original hypertoric variety, whose successive quotients recover the individual circle-weight spaces. We prove that the higher cohomology of the pre-quantum line orbibundle vanishes at every such level, so that the localised index is the character of the actual space of sections. Finally, a residual weight $x$ occurs at level $d$ if and only if $\mathcal{S}(x) \leq d$, where $\mathcal{S}$ is the arrangement slack function, with multiplicity $\binom{d - \mathcal{S}(x) + n}{n}$. Thus, each finite stage admits a weighted lattice-point description whose multiplicity function is supported on the lattice points in the support of the level-$d$ moment polyptych.

papers.title: Projective compactifications of hypersurface complements
papers.abstract: Let $U$ be a smooth affine variety of the form $U=\mathrm{P}^n\setminus H$, where $H\subset\mathrm{P}^n$ is a smooth connected hypersurface. We prove that every smooth projective compactification of the complex manifold $U$, by adding a smooth connected divisor, is isomorphic to $\mathrm{P}^n$. The proof uses the rational Reeb index of the normal circle bundle and positive $S^1$-equivariant symplectic homology. This paper is motivated by the work of Chi Li and Zhengyi Zhou, and makes a generalization to their result.

papers.title: An Unexpected Rational Blowdown
papers.abstract: The rational blowdown operation in 4-manifold topology replaces a neighborhood of a configuration of spheres by a rational homology ball. Such configurations typically arise from resolutions of surface singularities that admit rational homology disk smoothings. Conjecturally, all such singularities must be weighted homogeneous and belong to certain specific families: Stipsicz-Szab\'o--Wahl constructed QHD smoothings for these families and used Donaldson's theorem to obtain very restrictive necessary conditions on the resolution graphs for singularities with this property. In particular, these results, as well as subsequent work of Bhupal-Stipsicz, show that for certain resolution graphs, the canonical contact structure on the link of the singularity cannot admit a QHD symplectic filling. By contrast, we exhibit Stein rational homology disk fillings for the contact links of an infinite family of rational singularities that are not weighted homogeneous, producing a new symplectic rational blowdown. Inspiration for our construction comes from de Jong-van Straten's description of Milnor fibers of sandwiched singularities; we use the symplectic analog of de Jong-van Straten theory developed by the second and third authors. The unexpected Stein fillings are built using spinal open books and nearly Lefschetz fibrations.

papers.title: Symplectomorphism invariance of the wrapped Fukaya category
papers.abstract: An exact symplectomorphism of finite type Liouville manifolds is called 'strict' if it has bounded primitive; such symplectomorphisms are well known to induce deformation equivalences and hence equivalences of wrapped Fukaya categories. Here we note that an arbitrary symplectomorphism of Weinstein manifolds, with no assumptions at infinity, can be used to construct an equivalence of Fukaya categories. We combine this with a pointwise criterion for constructing such symplectomorphisms to improve two statements in the mirror symmetry literature -- for very affine hypersurfaces and multiplicative hypertoric varieties -- where Fukaya categories were calculated for a Liouville form not known to be strictly exact symplectomorphic to the natural K\"ahler Liouville form on the space in question. All results are obtained using ChatGPT Astra.

papers.title: Point-Splitting-Perturbative-Chern-Simons I
papers.abstract: We define mathematically the Point-Splitting Perturbative Chern-Simons Theory. The framing anomaly arise directly from the dependence of the configuration space of points on the frame.

papers.title: Point-Splitting-Perturbative-Chern-Simons II
papers.abstract: We extend the formalism of Point-Splitting-Perturbative-Chern-Simons to include Wilson Loops.

papers.title: Integral Points and Volume of Integral-Integral Affine Manifolds
papers.abstract: Using rational Ehrhart theory and Fourier analysis, we give an elementary proof that the volume of a closed manifold equipped with an integral-integral affine structure equals the number of its integral points.

papers.title: Sections, pseudosections, and multisections of Lefschetz fibrations
papers.abstract: We show that not every symplectic Lefschetz fibration over the $2$--sphere admits a smooth section, settling a long-standing open problem. To prove this, we develop a method for studying sections via lifts of monodromy factorizations with point-pushing maps and the induced handle decomposition of the total space, and apply it to an infinite family of Lefschetz fibrations. In contrast, we show that every Lefschetz fibration over $S^2$ admits positive multisections. Some of these examples admit no multisections with spherical components. We also construct signature-zero Lefschetz fibrations of every odd genus $g\geq 7$, which in turn give symplectic Lefschetz fibrations of any prescribed signature in each of these genera.

papers.title: Quantum Master Equation and Open Gromov-Witten Theory 2
papers.abstract: We define the not-abelian Open-Gromov-Witten partition function.
